## Install the kernel

A kernelspec belongs to the machine, so the usual choice is to install juphyter
once for your user, as [Installation](install.qmd) describes. Installing it as a
development dependency of one project pins the kernel's version with that
project, at the cost of a kernelspec that names that project's copy of the
engine:

```bash
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install
```

The command prints what the kernel is made of.

```
Installed the juphyter kernel "php" for PHP 8.5.10.
  kernel.json  /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php/kernel.json
  python       /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (ipykernel 7.4.0)
  php          /opt/homebrew/bin/php
  engine       /path/to/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/bin/juphyter
  quarto       /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (jupyter_client 8.10.0)
```

The Python is the interpreter that owns the `jupyter` on `PATH`, because the
kernel runs inside it. `--python` names a different one. The PHP is the binary
that runs the cells, and `--php` names a different one, which is how several
versions coexist:

```bash
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php
```

`juphyter uninstall --name php83` removes a kernelspec juphyter wrote, and
refuses to remove one it did not.

The `quarto` line appears when Quarto is installed. Quarto runs an interpreter
of its own choosing, and that one is the one that needs Jupyter in it, so the
line reports which interpreter that is and what was found there. When it says
`(no Jupyter)`, the kernelspec is still correct and `quarto render` cannot reach
it; [Installation](install.qmd) covers the fix.

On a machine with no Python that can host the kernel at all, the command offers
to build one. [Installation](install.qmd) covers that and the `--create-venv`
option that answers the offer in advance.

## A first cell

A cell is PHP without an opening tag. The value of the last expression is the
cell's result, and `echo` goes to the cell's output stream.

```{php}
$primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13];

echo count($primes), " primes, summing to ", array_sum($primes), "\n";

array_sum($primes) / count($primes);
```

State carries between cells, so the next cell sees what this one bound.

```{php}
$primes[] = 17;

$primes;
```

## Imports

A `use` statement applies to the cells after it as well as to its own. The
session accumulates them, so a notebook can put its imports in a first cell and
use short class names from then on.

```{php}
use DateTimeImmutable;

$released = new DateTimeImmutable('2026-11-20');

$released->format('F Y');
```

`namespace` is not supported in a cell, and a cell cannot redeclare a class or a
function that another cell already declared. PHP has no way to undefine either,
so a second run of a cell that declares one reports what it would have
redeclared rather than failing in the middle.

## Errors

A cell that throws reports the exception, its message, and the stack frames
that raised it, with each stack frame naming the cell and the line rather than
`eval()'d code`.

```{php}
#| error: true
$widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12];

$mean = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values);

$mean([]);
```

Warnings, notices, and deprecations go to the cell's error stream and leave the
cell running.

```{php}
$widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12];

$widths['narrow'] + $widths['medium'];
```

## Rich display

A value is published in every representation the front end might draw. A
phibble data frame comes with an HTML table and the tibble-style text phibble
prints at a terminal, and a phiz plot comes with a Vega-Lite specification, an
HTML embed, a static SVG when vl-convert is installed, and a one-line
description.

```{php}
#| echo: false
use Phibble\DataFrame;
```

```{php}
DataFrame::fromRows([
    ['package' => 'phibble', 'purpose' => 'data frames', 'version' => 0.3],
    ['package' => 'phplyr', 'purpose' => 'dplyr verbs', 'version' => 0.3],
    ['package' => 'phiz', 'purpose' => 'plots', 'version' => 0.3],
]);
```

Any class can opt in. A `toHtml(): string` method supplies the `text/html`
representation, and a `toMimeBundle(): array` method supplies the whole bundle.

```{php}
final class Progress
{
    public function __construct(private readonly int $done, private readonly int $total) {}

    public function toHtml(): string
    {
        return sprintf(
            '<progress value="%d" max="%d"></progress> %d of %d',
            $this->done,
            $this->total,
            $this->done,
            $this->total,
        );
    }

    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return sprintf('%d of %d', $this->done, $this->total);
    }
}

new Progress(7, 9);
```

`Juphyter\display()` publishes a value part way through a cell, so one cell can
show several data frames or plots.

```{php}
Juphyter\display(new Progress(3, 9));
Juphyter\display(new Progress(9, 9));
```
